analysis.title: GS US TMT .. 5 x 5 .. (Peter Callahan, 1 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The NDX is in its third 10%+ drawdown correction of 2026. Its roughly 7% decline in October was the second worst month since the AI cycle began in early 2023.

GS's Global Risk Appetite Indicator posted one of its largest monthly drops in 5+ years. The desk says the directional engine of the market (token demand and GW/data center build-outs) remains intact, but investors are more discerning about the linearity of the AI build-out beyond CY27, which pressures multiples.
The Monday-Wednesday bounce was faded. A benign FOMC meeting and robust 3Q earnings did not restart momentum in Tech/AI.

Investors are leaning toward broadening out the portfolio, but the desk says it does not sense a bearish directional tilt on AI suppliers. Broadening is hard because non-semis/AI names are exposed to AI disruption narratives, and AAPL, SNPS, ADI/TXN/NXPI, SPOT, V/MA, EBAY and LYV all traded poorly over the week or month.
Next week's catalysts are earnings from AAPL, NET, DDOG, AMD and ANET, plus the US midterm elections on 11/3. GIR expects the focus on data centers to fade somewhat after the election.

Top client inbounds: what happened Friday, new Mag 7 preferences, why MSFT faded, whether investors are cutting out-year estimates or only multiples in semis, the path for NOW after its print, whether the FTNT-driven security drawdown gets defended, setups into earnings, and whether e-commerce is inflecting (EBAY and ETSY cited AI growth tailwinds).

Several names had some of their worst post-earnings days ever (T+1): NOW -25%, INTC -30%, RDDT -30%, SNDK -13%, Eoptolink -15%, FFIV -20%, CAT -9%, Adyen -13%. The prior week's moves included TTMI -27% and LRCX -12%. The desk cites crowded positioning, a truncated calendar and ongoing secular debates as possible causes.
The desk lists names that pulled back or lagged out of earnings and have an idiosyncratic or out-of-consensus angle: TWLO, SNDK, RBLX, MSFT, AMZN, NOW, APH, Adyen, NXPI.

Semis (SOX) closed down about 7% on Friday and fell back below the 200-day moving average after 355 consecutive sessions above it (the 3rd longest streak in 10 years). The index is retesting the July low, and its forward P/E is back at AI-cycle lows of about 16x.
The desk says the rate-of-change datapoints from the week were all outside the AI complex, which remains a clear driver of strength. AMZN guided to two years of forward AWS revenue visibility.

Debated semis datapoints: Kioxia guided C4Q bit shipments flat q/q on timing (but said CY27 capacity is effectively sold out, as is most of 2028). MSFT capex came under budget in C3Q on third-party capacity delays (but guided to a 2H FY capex acceleration). INTC guided PC revenue down about 20% q/q in 4Q and expects the inventory correction to extend into 1H27 (but sees an accelerating server CPU market driven by agentic AI).
Eoptolink cited product delivery delays from flooding, uncertainty around VMI adoption and upstream supply tightness (e.g. DSP). AMKR and Vanchip gave weak smartphone read-outs.

AAPL enters Monday night's earnings at an all-time high multiple: 36x forward P/E, and a 17x premium to the S&P 500 on a relative basis. Focus areas are C3Q Services revenue growth, gross margin in the quarter and guidance, and the 4Q revenue guide. GIR expects guidance of low-to-mid single digit total revenue growth y/y.

UBER has sold off on 8 of its last 10 earnings prints at T+1 despite steady meets-and-beats, as investors struggle to price AVs and agentic commerce. It enters the print at about 10x EV/EBITDA and a P/E/G below 0.5x.
NET has had about 5 straight quarters of accelerating or stable revenue growth. Bulls hope momentum sustains into 2027+ as agentic activity grows on its platform (Workers, Pay per crawl).

MCHP: analog semis have de-rated over recent months despite ISM data near cycle highs. The desk asks whether MCHP can position the analog group as a core holding into 2027 after solid results from TXN and NXPI.
TTWO is described as one of the most idiosyncratic TMT names. The question is whether it can find support and re-base for a GTA 6 fueled year-end rally.

Calendar: Mon 11/2 US Manufacturing PMI (prev 54.5); Tue 11/3 JOLTS and midterms; Wed 11/4 US Services PMI and EU flash inflation; Thu 11/5 BoE rates decision; Fri 11/6 US NFP (prev +29k). Heavy earnings each day.
